newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crude prices firm in late Asia, Bach Ho steady.
newsitem.headline: Crude prices firm in late Asia, Bach Ho steady.

text.p: Crude oil prices were firm in the late Asian market on Friday, traders said.
They said a handful of June Bach Ho crudes were believed to have been done recently at firm levels in the wet market.
June cash Brent was notionally assessed at $18.65/18.75 per barrel in late afternoon Tokyo trading. At 0940 GMT, June Brent was most recently traded at $18.76 and July Brent at $18.74 on SIMEX.
In spreads, July Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at 90 cents/$1.00.
In the wet market, four June Bach Ho crude oil cargoes were believed to have been exchanged this week. Some were said to have been done at fairly strong premiums.

The cargoes were all reported to have been sold by Japanese trading companies, with two June Bach Ho cargoes believed done at a premium of 25 cents to the official selling price. The remaining two were said to have been done at a premium of 19 cents and 30 cents respectively. The volume ranged from 100,000 to 450,000 barrels. The buyers included traders and majors.
In regional crudes, a 150,000 barrel May Minas was believed to have been sold by a Japanese trading company to a major.
The Minas was believed to have been sold at a premium of 10 cents to the official selling price, representing a decline from earlier deals, traders said.
In Middle East crudes, traders estimated that about two to three million barrels of Abu Dhabi grade crudes, including Murban, Umm Shaif and Lower Zakum, were still looking for buyers.
They said there was a vague rumour that a European major had swapped a Lower Zakum for a Murban. Traders said that the Murban cargo would probably be taken to Kenya.
